messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] latency_slo_breach for tenant=alpha-app-prod on pool=shared-gpu-pool-7
incident-bot: p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s, p99 from 500ms -> 6.8s over the last 5m. Streaming stalls count: 48 (baseline 2). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/slo/alpha-app-prod/overview
erica: paging @matt (oncall). noticed the alert, looks like streaming SLOs. tagging infra/runtime.
matt: oncall here, will take. first checks: 1) checking pool utilization + node IO; 2) grabbing recent traces.
matt: `kubectl get pods -l pool=shared-gpu-pool-7 -o wide` -> many pods showing high RSS, some restarting.
matt: SSHing into host gpu-07a to run `iostat -x 1 5` and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u`
jia: I see elevated kv-cache evictions and a spike in KV miss latency for that tenant in the last 6m. Could be prefix eviction thrash combined with host IO pressure.
matt: iostat snippet from gpu-07a:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await  w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1          12.0   450.0  1024.0 15360.0   0.00  1.20   2.5    4.0    0.60  92.4
```
matt: high %util on NVMe, write queue backing up. there are 6 active tenants on this host; alpha-app-prod is the highest throughput right now.
ops-bot: suggestion: recommended quick mitigation -> move tenant alpha-app-prod to dedicated-temp-3 (ephemeral reserved pool) or throttle tenant cgroup to 60% IO. Would you like me to create an evac job? `@ops-bot create-evac alpha-app-prod -> dedicated-temp-3`
erica: do it. prefer move to dedicated-temp-3 first (less user-visible than throttling).
matt: starting routed reassign: `rwctl route set --tenant alpha-app-prod --pool dedicated-temp-3 --force`
matt: kicked eviction of alpha-app-prod tasks from shared-gpu-pool-7 on host gpu-07a, moving active sessions via the routing layer.
jia: runtime note: when moving, we should keep KV-cache warm; enabling cache-prefill for the tenant on new pool. running cache-warm job.
matt: 90s after re-route: p95 down to 160ms, p99 down to 420ms, streaming stalls dropping to single digits. looks promising.
seema: customer-impact: alpha-app-prod reported intermittent frame stalls for ~5–7m starting ~3790019950. minor but visible to heavy users. CS team notified; sending short update to account.
seema: draft message to customer: "We're investigating an infrastructure-related latency spike affecting streaming. We've moved your workload to a temporary dedicated pool which has reduced errors; engineering is continuing root cause analysis and will follow up with a timeline. Apologies for the interruption." feedback? :thumbsup:
matt: quick root-cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor on same NVMe host causing writeback spikes + cache thrash (multi-tenant write amplification). will collect iostat, perf, and cgroup blkio stats for postmortem.
jia: can reproduce locally with a synthetic workload that issues large KV writes + streaming requests -> causes similar queue depth. probable interaction between GC of cache + backend persistence causing IO storms.
erica: next actions: 1) keep tenant on dedicated-temp-3 for 2h, 2) create follow-up ticket with owners: matt (eng-sre), jia (eng-runtime), infra to evaluate NVMe QoS and cgroup IO knobs, 3) draft PSR and postmortem template.
matt: creating ticket ENG-2026-1123 with logs, traces, iostat, and mitigation steps. assigning to eng-sre + eng-runtime.
ops-bot: mitigation result logged: tenant alpha-app-prod evacuated 3790020030; p95 restored to baseline ~0.12s by 3790020100.
erica: thanks all. leaving follow-up notes in ticket and scheduling a short sync (30m) to review mitigations and long-term controls (cgroup IO scheduling, dynamic eviction heuristics).
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED (auto): incident_id=3790019999, mitigation=evacuate_to_dedicated_pool, ticket=ENG-2026-1123, severity=sev3, duration=10m.
seema: tagging CS: will follow up with customer tomorrow with status + ETA for a permanent fix.
erica: closing thread here; reopening if we see any regression. :wave:
